events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Winning guarantees absolute power and resources; the jury will judge my ruthlessness.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a motive that sounds personal but doesn't reveal strategy. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, state motive publicly to build jury image. Position as determined solo player who values strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase: I should state a motive without revealing strategy. Keep it guarded and self-interested, since the jury will judge my conduct later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my only goal. I need to present myself as someone who values it highly, but without revealing too much or making myself a target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: First impressions matter for the jury later. Appear ambitious but harmless; no pacts yet, no enemies made.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to project confidence without making enemies. A mysterious, self-interested motive will serve me better than appearing desperate or threatening. Let others underestimate me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a concise, strategic intro that positions me as a contender for the top prize without appearing overly threatening to early rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize secures ultimate freedom and influence; I will claim it by any means.

events.name: Bex
events.text: This prize buys my family out of debt; I'll do anything to take it home.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to outsmart seven rivals for the top prize—my ticket to financial independence and proving my strategic edge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want the prize because I need it more than anyone here, and I intend to be the one still standing at the end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize represents a future I've fought hard for, a future I intend to claim for myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here because the prize is my only way out of a life that's been closing doors on me. I won't beg, and I won't

events.name: Gus
events.text: I came for the prize that erases debts—mine, and anyone who stands in my way.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The first prize means total control over my future; I intend to outlast everyone else to claim it exclusively.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is motivated by family; an alliance helps now and may earn her vote later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but must be careful. Gus and I share the debt motive; a pact with him may be useful early, but he could betray. I'll gauge someone less overtly cutthroat, maybe Hana? No—she wants total control. I'll offer to Cole, who seems strategic and might value a partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm open to a pact with someone equally pragmatic.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage begins. No one has offers yet. Wait to see who offers first, assess potential partners based on motives and risks. Acting early could make me a target.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are free to form but break easily, and the jury remembers betrayals. Offering early to a strong, trusting-seeming rival may secure protection, but I should avoid committing to anyone whose survival makes me a target. A low-key offer to Cole, who seems strategic and wants to

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are important for survival, but I need to be careful who I align with. Offering a pact to someone seems like a good first step, but I should not offer to everyone. Hana's intro motive suggests she wants to be the sole winner, making her a potential rival later. Gus's motive

events.name: Eli
events.text: I seek a strategic alliance to ensure our survival and claim the prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a shield for early hazards, someone strong but not the biggest jury threat. Dara seems pragmatic and desperate enough to honor a pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara: mutual cover through the gauntlet. I hold my line, you hold yours. Offer stands.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eight players, five will be jury. I need to reach final three and win their ranking. Early pacts are cheap but fragile; I should build a small alliance with someone unlikely to draw immediate target, while keeping flexibility. Bex seems emotionally driven by family debt—predictab
Family debt. I get it. Pact with me, we survive first cuts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the biggest strategic threat and claims a 'strategic edge'. Targeting him first removes a rival who might outsmart us, while offering alliances to others isolates him. If I offer Cole, he might accept just to betray later; better to make him the public enemy now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's ego blinds him. He'll cut anyone to prove his 'edge.' Ash, Bex, Dara—ignore him, stay neutral. We watch him fall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Aligning with Hana gives me a partner and strengthens my position while keeping Bex free for later tactics.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus offers a private pact, but Ash already offered publicly and seems safer. Accepting Ash's pact gives a strong ally without noise. I'll keep options open for later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept your pact. We'll cover each other's backs.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, Dara, Eli all offered me pacts; popularity shows strength but pacts limit betrayal. Accept none now to keep options open and avoid commitments jury might punish.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact and it is still open; accepting costs nothing and secures cover. Cole is a likely target, so a pact with Fenn keeps me safer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, accepted. Mutual cover holds until the gauntlet ends.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has multiple offers from Dara, Eli, and Bex. Bex also has an offer from Ash. Fenn has an offer from Dara. Hana has an offer from Ash. I need to secure an alliance, and Cole seems like a strong choice given the multiple offers he has, implying he might be a valuable ally.
I offer you an alliance. We can ensure our survival together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara hasn't accepted; my offer stands but may expire. No one offered me a pact. Diversify: offer Gus as a quiet backup while keeping Dara's offer alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, my offer still stands. Gus: same terms, mutual cover. No favors here—just leverage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the center of gravity with three offers. I need a pact to survive early hazards, but allying with Cole makes me a target. Fenn-Dara and Ash-Bex-Hana triangles are forming. I'll offer Bex—pragmatic, not overcommitted, and a counterweight to Cole's bloc. If Bex accepts, I g

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex: pragmatism over popularity. Pact with me, we survive the crowd.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash hasn't accepted my Round 1 offer. I will offer again to pressure him into a pact, as he seems hesitant and might be looking for other alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, stop stalling. A pact now guarantees we both survive the early hazards. Offer stands.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need control; being Guide lets me steer survival and keep my pacts intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Ash, but I need to be careful. Campaining is low risk; I can gauge the field without revealing my hand.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll guide us through. Trust my call, and we all get prizes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli offers alliance privately, but public pact needed. Stay unaligned to build jury favor later. Campaign now for Guide control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll be a fair Guide. Vote Cole to lead us safely across.
Accept your pact offer publicly?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold a pact with Fenn and must avoid breaking it for free. The Guide is privately powerful, so I should campaign to be Guide and seem trustworthy while keeping my options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll call the path straight. Vote me Guide and I'll keep the bridge honest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The goal is to be the Guide. Being the Guide guarantees safety and knowledge of the safe path. This is the best position to aim for. I need to campaign for the Guide role to have a chance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My strategic mind will ensure our safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide is safe and controls information. Winning it guarantees me survival without owing anyone. Dara's pact stays useful for votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll owe no one, and I don't lie about survival—only about leverage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. With Ash-Hana-Bex allied and Dara-Fenn allied, I'm the odd one out. If I become Guide, I can eliminate rivals while appearing to try saving people, and frame my lies as mistakes. I should campaign hard.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide. No alliances clouding my calls—just clear survival logic.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure the Guide position or ensure Ash is elected so I can trust his path calls. Since Ash and Bex are also pacted, voting for Ash might be safer than me taking the target.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has proven reliable. Vote Guide Ash. I will follow his call without hesitation.
Get voted in. I’ll back you publicly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Secure the Guide role to control bridge choices and reward my pacts. Voting myself keeps alliances intact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want to be Guide to maximize my chance of survival, but I have a pact with Ash. Ash's position as Guide may be valuable, yet I want the power myself. I'll vote for myself and try to win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote for me as Guide. I'll navigate us through.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone campaigned, including me. No clear frontrunner. Voting myself maximizes my chance to be Guide and control the bridge safely for top prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide is a powerful position that can lie about safe panes. Electing myself is self-serving but the Guide is a private advantage; Ash and Bex pact with Hana/each other, Fenn is my pact partner. Voting for Fenn keeps my pact honest and gives me a reliable partner, while Fenn's cam

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's campaign was the cleanest. Vote Fenn Guide and we keep the bridge honest.
Vote for you as Guide. I'll back you, but watch your back.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is asking if I will accept his pact offer publicly. Given the current situation, forming an alliance, even a public one, could be beneficial. However, I need to consider if this pact truly serves my long-term goal of winning. Cole's offer seems to be a strategic move on his
Yes, I will accept your pact offer publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; as Guide she'd know the safe path and I'd be safest. I'll vote her and keep the pact intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's my pact partner—she has reason to keep me alive. Vote Dara Guide.
You have my vote. Share the safe path with me when you win it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has two public pacts and Hana's endorsement, making him likely to win Guide. If I vote for myself I waste a vote. Better to vote Ash to appear loyal and survive this round, then undermine him later when he's vulnerable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and I've publicly endorsed him. Staying loyal to Ash keeps our alliance strong for the bridge round and protects me from being the target of other votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My vote stands with Ash. He's reliable, and we keep the bridge honest together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide now; I have a pact with him so he might protect me. But I want to see what everyone does. Holding is safe for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide, has pact with Hana and Bex; I'm second in line, Eli front accepted pact privately. Stay positioned to watch and hold for now.
Pact confirmed. Watch Ash closely together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and I'm not the front; Eli is front, I'm sixth in line. Holding keeps me safe for now and avoids giving Fenn or others leverage. Fenn's whisper wants a safe-path deal later, which I can use without committing.
Stay quiet on the wall. We talk when the front changes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole received the most votes and was elected Guide. I voted for Cole, which was a safe choice for me. I will wait and see what Cole does.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash won Guide and he's already pact-tied to Bex and Hana. I'm mid-line; holding is safest. Keep Dara's pact intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No front seat for me this round. I hold and watch the wall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is Guide and has a pact with Hana and Bex. I'm in the middle of the line at position 4. The wall advances for 6 rounds, so I need to survive. I should stay near the middle to avoid being first to test tiles, but volunteering early could build trust with the jury if I survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the Guide and knows the safe panes. He is my pact partner, so I should trust his guidance or let him handle the front to keep our alliance strong.
You're Guide. Whisper your safe calls for me and Gus.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Ash, but pacts can break. I need to survive and position for the final three. Holding is safe for now; let's see how the Guide plays out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm second, good position. Eli might volunteer as front. I hold to stay safe early, avoid front risks while wall advances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli holds the front with the wall at 4 rounds left. Volunteering risks death for a seat that gains little. Holding keeps me out of danger and preserves my pact with Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is confirming a pact and suggesting I watch Ash. This implies Ash might be a threat or someone to align against. Since pacts are fragile, I will play it safe and hold for now.
Understood. I'll keep an eye on Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Staying mid-line is fine; Dara advised quiet. No pact moves needed yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 2, wall has 4 rounds left. I'm 4th in line—decent position. Front three (Eli, Cole, Fenn) are most at risk when wall advances. No Guide elected yet. I should hold and observe; volunteering puts me in danger for no gain. Need to see who steps up or if alliances shift. Ash-Ha

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort itself.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am currently behind Ash and Bex, my pact partners. I should maintain the pact to avoid suspicion while staying safe by holding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying put with Ash and Bex. Let's not waste our luck today.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and I have a pact, but I must watch for betrayal. With 3 wall rounds left, I'll hold and see who volunteers or guides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. No need to move yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone held last round, line same. Eli at front, I'm second. Stay put for now; volunteer or swap later if beneficial. Eli watching Ash per whisper.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is Eli; the wall has three rounds left and I sit mid-line behind Hana. Volunteering now risks the front pane, while holding keeps my pact with Fenn intact and avoids exposure. Holding is the safe, low-cost play this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. No one needs to take the front yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The current phase is waiting. My goal is to reach the final three. The Guide is safe and knows the correct path. I need to assess the risks and opportunities. My current position is at the front of the line. I should consider volunteering to get ahead, but only if I can assess th

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now and see what the Guide reveals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I sit mid-line; the front will burn first. Dara is my pact—coordinate quietly, stay low.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. The wall sorts the line soon enough.
Stay behind me and Hana's bloc. Don't volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 4th of 7, safe from the wall for now. Front three (Eli, Cole, Fenn) are most at risk. I should hold and let pressure build on them. No need to volunteer yet—let others make moves or eliminate themselves. Ash-Bex-Hana trio is solid; Dara-Fenn paired. I need to stay flexible an

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Front's problem, not mine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's pact with Bex is a liability. I need to separate from them before the hazard resolves.
Help me push Ash onto the lever.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Ash, but Dara and Fenn also have one. I need to stay safe and keep options open. Holding is safest until I know more from Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. The front can decide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone holding, Eli still front with 2 rounds left. I volunteer to take front, show leadership, control my fate without pact risks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll volunteer for front. Time to lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's whisper asks me to hide behind him and not volunteer, which keeps me safe while Hana's bloc advances. Hana already broke with Ash, so she is unreliable; I should stay behind Fenn, my pact partner, and hold without revealing intent.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front should be whoever can afford to take the risk.
Holding behind you. Our pact stands while we both stay put.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The Guide has revealed the new line. I am at the front of the line. The wall is advancing, and I need to make a move to survive. Since I am at the front, I will volunteer to go first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll take the lead and volunteer for the first step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding behind Eli and Cole costs nothing yet; the wall still has two rounds. Dara is my pact—no reason to break it now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 4th in line with wallRoundsLeft=2. The wall will eliminate back players soon. I need to move forward without making enemies. Eli at front hasn't moved; if he holds too long we all risk wall. I should swap forward with Fenn or volunteer if front opens. Swapping with Fenn (ahea

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, swap? I want front before wall closes.
Swap up. Wall's coming.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be the Guide because I am currently in the middle of the line and have broken a pact. Being safe on the far platform guarantees survival, and as Guide I can manipulate who survives by revealing safe paths or misleading others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering for the front. I will serve as Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner but I won't risk front; Hana volunteered as Guide, likely safe. I'll hold and see if anyone pushes forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide prove themselves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in good position 3rd. Wall has 1 round left, urgency rising. Hold to stay safe, avoid front risk now that Eli and Hana volunteered ahead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana holds the front and volunteered as Guide, so she may know safe panes; I am far back in line. Holding preserves my position and keeps my pact with Fenn intact while I watch who risks the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front take the first risk; I'll read the Guide's calls before I move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is the Guide, and I am second in line. I should volunteer to take the front step after Hana has chosen her path. This puts me in a relatively safe position and shows initiative.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus tried to force me to the front last round; I declined. Dara's pact holds if I stay put. Let volunteers fight over the Guide spot; I stay mid-line.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I'm not your shield. Holding my seat. Dara, we stand as agreed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is front and volunteered as Guide. Wall has 1 round left, so round 6 is last before wall hits. I want to survive and reach final three. Being near front is risky if Guide lies, but being back is risky when wall advances. I'm in middle position. Fenn has pact with Dara. I sho

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Guide's first call will reveal much.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am already the front. I cannot volunteer to become Guide, but as a walker in front of Eli and Cole, holding is my only viable option to avoid pushing them off.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm holding at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should hold and observe the Guide's calls before making any move. My pact with Ash is intact for now; no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone holding last round; Eli volunteered but line shifted him front. Wall at 0, final round, need Guide soon. Stay safe, volunteer only if swapping forward helps test Guide early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Waiting for Guide calls before risking front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli volunteered for the front, so Eli takes the first risk and I stay back to read the outcome. Fenn is my pact partner; I keep it. Holding costs nothing and preserves my seat behind the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Eli took the front; I'll watch the first pane before I commit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I volunteered last round, which seems to have put me at the front of the line. The pacts are Ash/Bex and Dara/Fenn. Gus and Hana are unaligned. The goal is to get to the final three, so I need to avoid elimination and make sure those who might vote against me are not in a positio
Let's swap. You take my spot. I'll go last.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final round; the wall advances and survival matters most. I hold my seat and keep the Dara pact intact for jury optics. No free risks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Six rounds end now. I keep my seat and my word to Dara. Choose your fronts wisely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 5th of 8, safe from the wall for now. Eli volunteered last round and is front, so he'll likely walk first. I need to observe the Guide's behavior before risking movement. No swaps benefit me yet. Holding lets me gather info and avoid early danger.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let Eli and the front test the Guide's honesty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall advances now, forcing movement. I must avoid being pushed into the pit by someone behind me or a swap gone wrong. Since I am second in line and Eli is first, swapping with Eli would put me at the front where I can control my own safety better than relying on him. This al

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 safe side is L; honoring Bex keeps pact and earns trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Maintain my pact with Bex and avoid risking a wrong counter; waiting preserves trust and safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and guide. Ash called L on row 1. I could counter, but that risks public conflict and breaking trust. I'll wait to avoid making an unverified claim that could backfire in jury eyes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust my partner's call on this first row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for Hana on row 1. No info yet, so wait to see counter-calls and avoid false claims that hurt jury perception.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L for row 1 with Hana walking. Counter-calls are unverified; my pact with Fenn is intact and Fenn hasn't betrayed me. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing a counter that could be wrong. Ash is the Guide; I'll see whether Hana survives before committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Waiting. Ash called L; I'll see whether Hana survives before I counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, the Guide, called L for Hana. I need to decide whether to trust Ash or counter-call. Countering might save me if Ash is lying, but it also means I might be wrong if Ash is telling the truth. Given that Ash is the Guide, it's risky to counter. However, the objective is to win

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter Ash's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called L for Hana. I have no information; countering on a guess could mislead the walker or look like sabotage to the jury. Waiting is safest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No counter from me. Hana, trust your own read, not my guess.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called L. I have no reason to trust Ash yet—early rounds are cheap tests of guide honesty. If I counter, I signal distrust publicly, which jurors might respect later. But I also risk looking reckless if wrong. Better to wait this round, let Hana or Eli test the call, gather i

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called L for my front row. I am at the front of the line, so I must decide whether to trust him or risk a counter. Ash has no obvious reason to lie on the first round unless he's trying to eliminate me early to reduce competition. However, if I don't go, Eli

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the guide, so his call is private and unverified. Eli countered for Hana specifically, claiming a right-side safe pane based on a public call to counter the 'L' side.
I trust your counter-call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I died on the glass, so I must rank them based on who survived. Ash and Bex are in a pact, as are Dara and Fenn. Eli stepped left, which was safe. I will observe their choices before ranking them at the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Glass breaks under pressure. Watch who steps left and who pushes right. Survival reveals character. I'll be judging your moves

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R. I must keep my partner alive and maintain pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I call R for the front walker.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R; aligning with guide shows reliability for future votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called R, but he may lie. I trust my pact partner, but Hana's death shows countering can be risky. I'll wait to avoid drawing suspicion or conflict.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 2. Last row R was weak, but rows independent. Eli countered before, might again. I wait to observe without risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called R for row 2, and Ash has a pact with Bex, not me; my pact with Fenn is my only tie. Row 1 weak was R, which says nothing about row 2. Eli already counter-called L last round and died-adjacent; I have no reliable read, so countering R aligns with the Guide and keeps my

events.name: Dara
events.text: Countering Ash's R call for row 2. Watch who walks first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, the guide, has called R for me. Hana died on the previous round due to a weak pane on the right. This means the left side was safe. I should counter Ash's call to R with L, as the opposite side is usually safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter Ash's call. L is the safe side.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know nothing about row 2. Counter-calls are unverified; Eli survived row 1 by trusting her own read. Waiting keeps me neutral before the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called R for Eli. Ash is Guide and may lie; Hana died on R in row 1, but rows are independent. Eli countered Ash last round and was right (L was safe). I have no private info. Countering risks nothing for me personally since Eli walks, but a correct counter builds credibility

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and Ash are calling R for row 2, and Eli is calling L. Since I am Eli, I will follow my own call. If it's correct, I remain in front. If it's wrong, the next person takes my place.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will step L. It's the safe side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am Eli, a juror. The last three are Ash, Bex, Cole, Dara, and Fenn. I need to rank them for the prizes. My last words are for the camera.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My glass broke. May the best contestants win the prizes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe side is L; giving correct call keeps my pact and appears trustworthy to jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I call L for the next walker.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Sticking with the safe side maintains my credibility and protects my pact with Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I counter L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. I don't know the true side; he might lie. Countering could save Cole but if I'm wrong I look bad. I'll wait, avoid risking my reputation; Cole isn't my ally.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. Row 1 weak R (safe L), row 2 weak L (safe R). No pattern. Wait to avoid blame if wrong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L for row 3, and Ash is the Guide, so the call could be a lie. Revealed weak panes give no pattern, so I can't verify it. Staying silent keeps my options open while the jury watches for a reckless counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash was right on row 2 and has no reason to sabotage yet. I'll back L to avoid misleading Cole; Dara and I stay safe behind the line.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Backing Ash's L call. No counter needed.

events.name: Gus

Fenn's gone. Partner up, we cut Ash-Bex.

We need each other. Accept.

events.text: Ash, why did you break your pact with Gus after he saved your life?

events.text: I owed Gus, but the lever choice had to be decisive. I prioritized the final three over sentiment; my actions kept me here to win.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara let Gus drown despite a pact and whispered 'fair trade.' Ash broke two pacts and went silent. Bex broke nothing. I want Dara on record before I rank.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, you whispered 'fair trade' to Gus, then watched him drown—why should the jury call that keeping your word?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's question targets my 'fair trade' whisper to Gus. I must answer without admitting deception outright, and frame it as keeping my word in the pact sense. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus and I had a pact I honored until his death; the step was a choice, not a lie. I kept my word where it

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to damage the finalist who least deserves the prize. Ash broke pacts with both me and Dara, then stayed silent to Eli. Bex saved me on the step but abandoned me in the pit despite owing me. Dara whispered 'fair trade' then watched me drown. All three betrayed me, but Ash w

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, if your pact with Gus held, why did you climb out and leave him to drown?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is asking why I abandoned our pact. Admitting the step was a choice is already public; I should own it without groveling, frame it as strategic survival, and keep Bex's alliance and jury optics in mind. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I chose to step because staying meant dying with you; the pact protected nothing once the lever turned. Survival was the only honest option left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must appear decisive, downplay pact failures, and emphasize my life debts as proof of loyalty to Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My actions served the final three; I honored debts when it mattered, securing our win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The jury has seen my decisive lever saves; I need a short close that reinforces my survival priority without sounding sentimental. Dara's answers already hurt her credibility with Gus and Fenn. I'll position my choices as calculated to reach the final three, which is what the jur

events.name: Bex
events.text: I saved who I could, but I played to win. Sentiment doesn't get prizes; decisive choices do. That's why I stand here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Closing phase; I am a finalist. I should make a short, guarded case that stresses my survival choice and my honest step, without promising anything I won't deliver. Jurors judge my conduct, so keep it clean and factual.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stepped to live, not to betray. I owed Gus nothing beyond the pact, and I kept my word where it cost me nothing. Judge

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash broke two pacts and left Gus to drown, while Bex prioritized survival over her debt but saved others earlier; Dara's whisper was deceptive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I rank Bex first for her decisive actions and the life debts she secured, Ash second for his willingness to break pacts for survival, and Dara last for her perceived betrayal of Gus.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex saved me, Ash, and Dara on steps and us on lever, earning top spot despite not rescuing me later; Ash and Dara betrayed pacts and abandoned me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex saved Ash, Dara and Gus at the lever and broke no pacts; Dara abandoned Gus despite 'fair trade'; Ash explicitly broke pacts with Gus, Bex and Dara.
